moat_against: Fragmented market with strong direct rivals — Geotab (ABI Research's top-ranked commercial telematics vendor, Samsara second), Motive, Verizon Connect, PowerFleet
Hardware commoditization and OEM-embedded telematics erode the installed-base advantage over time
No proven pricing power into profitability — SBC-funded talent model has kept owner's earnings negative at every scale so far; physical-operations customers are cost-sensitive and cyclical
moat_for: Installed hardware + cloud platform in vehicles/assets — replacing it means re-instrumenting fleets, retraining, and losing historical data
Multi-product platform breadth (telematics, video safety, equipment, sites, workflows) driving expansion inside large accounts — $1M+ ARR cohort over $500M ARR, +50%+ YoY
Scale data asset — ARR $2.125B growing +30% at 77% GAAP gross margin (Q2 FY2027), funding AI features smaller rivals cannot match as easily
moat_justification: A broad, scaled connected-operations platform — installed telematics/camera hardware, years of operational data, and workflow integration create real switching costs, and multi-product expansion inside large accounts is visible in the prints ($1M+ ARR cohort ARR over $500M, up over 50% YoY). Not 7+: the fleet-management market is fragmented (top-10 vendors ~13% of revenue), Geotab and Motive contest the same fleets, hardware is commoditizing / OEM-embedding, and Samsara has never converted its position into positive owner's earnings or proven returns on capital through a cycle.
name: Samsara Inc.
one_liner: Strong connected-operations platform, moat 6/10, revenue +30% at $2.125B ARR — but SBC ($330.6M TTM) exceeds TTM operating cash flow ($288.4M), so owner's earnings are negative on every basis (median -$0.30/sh, TTM -$0.13/sh) and it cannot clear 15% at $40.50; Tier F until SBC normalizes.
